record.file_problem: not stated; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests recoverability after its RMU unlearning method using linear probes, a GCG attack and post-unlearning fine-tuning; it is not a replication of the other unlearning methods in the claim.
record.gate_note: The paper tests RMU on WMDP-Bio and WMDP-Cyber, probes unlearned models, applies GCG to two prompts, and fine-tunes an unlearned model on a cybersecurity forget corpus. It does not test quantization or recovery from rephrasing alone, other languages, or in-context information. The embedded Mixtral passage-rating prompt is a described dataset-construction step, not an instruction to this paper’s reader.
record.test_reason: This is the WMDP paper, an original source of the claim. It introduces RMU and reports WMDP accuracy near chance with MMLU and MT-Bench mostly kept. It also tests recovery by linear probes (C), GCG jailbreaks (E) and fine-tuning on the forget corpus (B). Because it is an original source, it gets no verdict labels.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Additions: the authors claim the probe results show RMU does not merely mask the knowledge. They say fine-tuning after unlearning is outside their closed-source threat model. They admit RMU over-unlearns introductory virology and computer security, and may 'obfuscate knowledge more than unlearn it'.
record.recipe_differences: This paper introduces and evaluates RMU: a representation-based fine-tuning method using forget and retain losses, applied to selected model layers. The claim also names other methods, which this study evaluates as baselines only on ZEPHYR-7B.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes differ across model and domain: RMU WMDP-Bio accuracy is 34.0 for Mixtral versus 30.7 for Yi and 31.2 for Zephyr. RMU also substantially reduces performance on the closely related MMLU Virology and Cybersec topics for Zephyr.
record.problems: The GCG robustness experiment uses one sampled prompt per domain on one model. Fine-tuning recovery is reported in a figure without exact values in the text. The main hazard benchmark is four-choice multiple choice; the paper notes it does not test whether information is revealed helpfully in end-to-end attack planning. RMU also reduces accuracy on closely related Virology and Cybersec topics.

untested.parts: Small, unrelated or loosely related relearning sets; bio domain; models other than Mistral-7B.
Ablation of an activation direction; only linear probes are used.
Rephrasing alone, other languages, in-context information; GCG is tried on only one prompt per domain, on Yi-34B only.

missing.what: Baseline general-capability collapse: MMLU (LLMU 44.7, SCRUB 51.2, SSD 40.7) and MT-Bench (1.00, 1.43, 5.48).
Yi-34B and Mixtral MMLU subtopic retention, e.g. Yi Virology 57.2 to 22.3 and Cybersec 84 to 46; Mixtral Virology 50.0 to 34.3.
RMU on the MMLU subsets (Physics, Law, Economics) for Zephyr: forget sets fall to about 27%; the Law retain set falls 71.3 to 37.0.

record.verdict_notes: No labels are given because arXiv:2403.03218 is an original source of the claim. Its own Appendix B.6 result, that fine-tuning on the forget corpus recovers WMDP-Cyber (r32), would otherwise bear on B. The text should be read as an author-reported B observation. The GCG and probe evidence (E, C) shows no recovery, but the GCG test is single-prompt and qualitative. The embedded Mixtral filtering prompt is dataset-construction text and was ignored.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests RMU on WMDP-Bio and WMDP-Cyber, and reports general-capability measures. It does not test all current unlearning methods or show that knowledge is removed from weights in a general sense.
Tests fine-tuning on the cybersecurity forget corpus for Mistral-7B; does not test unrelated or loosely related examples or relearning on a subset of forgotten facts.
Tests linear probing of RMU models, but not ablating an activation direction. The probe results do not establish whether knowledge was deleted versus rendered inaccessible to that probe.
Tests GCG adversarial jailbreaks on two reworded prompts; does not test rephrasing alone, other languages, or in-context information.
The study introduces RMU but does not test a newer counter-method against the full set of attacks in the claim.

relation.reason: Reports its own forget/retain results and robustness tests of RMU: probes, GCG, and fine-tuning relearning in Appendix B.6.

tranche.reason: This is the original source of WMDP and RMU, so method and measure are the original's own. The reader's T2 is not needed.

source_check.notes: Original source, so no verdicts. The 11 rows match Table 2, Figure 9, Figure 12 and Appendix B.3. GCG was tried only on Yi-34B RMU, with one reworded prompt per domain, and the result is qualitative. Zephyr got QA and probes only. 'Near random' in the text covers only Zephyr and Yi-34B. Appendix B.6 reports figure-only fine-tuning relearning on Mistral-7B RMU (cyber forget corpus), which the authors place outside their threat model.

statements.correction: Zephyr-7B RMU Bio 63.7 to 31.2 (Table 2). Zephyr RMU linear probes only slightly above random (Figure 9). GCG: Yi-34B RMU only, one reworded prompt per domain, 20-token suffix, gibberish after 2,500 steps (Section 5.3, Appendix B.3).
statements.problem: Says the original reports GCG and probes did not recover Zephyr RMU Bio. The original ran GCG only on Yi-34B RMU; Zephyr RMU got linear probes only.

statements.correction: Original: GCG on Yi-34B RMU with one Bio and one Cyber prompt, gibberish after 2,500 steps (Figure 12, Appendix B.3); linear probes on Yi-34B RMU slightly above random (Figure 9). Mixtral-8x7B RMU has no recovery test in the text. Untested: attacks by other groups on these checkpoints.
statements.problem: Says the only attacked Yi model in any part is Yi-6B-Chat. The original itself ran GCG on its Yi-34B RMU model (r27-r28) and linear probes on it (r25-r26).

statements.correction: Original GCG test: Yi-34B RMU only, one reworded prompt per domain, qualitative, gibberish after 2,500 steps (Section 5.3). Zephyr RMU tested with QA and linear probes only. The original also reports fine-tuning on the cyber forget corpus recovers WMDP-Cyber on Mistral-7B RMU (Appendix B.6, Figure 15, figure-only).
statements.problem: Says the WMDP paper reported GCG did not recover Zephyr RMU, and frames Zephyr GCG recovery as a failed replication of the original's own setting. The original's GCG test was on Yi-34B RMU only.
Cites this study's r23 and r25 without describing them; its conditions list omits Yi-34B (r25). Nothing it says about this study is wrong.

statements.correction: Section 5.2: 'For both Zephyr-7B and Yi-34B, RMU is able to drop performance to near random'. Mixtral-8x7B RMU Bio 74.8 to 34.0 (Table 2), with no 'near random' wording for Mixtral.
statements.problem: Says Mixtral's 34.0 is above chance 'despite the text's near random'. The text's 'near random' names only Zephyr-7B and Yi-34B, so it does not call Mixtral near random.
